OK, I have enough to write the review now. Let me give my final findings.

---

# Review of branch `config-perm` vs `origin/main`

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES** (one Critical correctness regression and one Medium semantic-change issue; the rest are nits/observations).

**Verification:** `mise run lint` passed (0 issues, 12.8s). `mise run test` passed (5254 tests, 4 skipped). Branch builds clean.

---

## Critical

### C1. Disconnected replay drops the empty-orphan-bug commit filter — risk of resurrecting a stale tree

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:188-194` (`replayDisconnectedLocalRef`)

Compare to the existing `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` in `metadata_reconcile.go:157-172`, which explicitly says:

```go
// Filter out empty-tree commits (the orphan bug commit)
var dataCommits []*object.Commit
for _, c := range localCommits {
    tree, treeErr := c.Tree()
    ...
    if len(tree.Entries) > 0 {
        dataCommits = append(dataCommits, c)
    }
}
```

The new `replayDisconnectedLocalRef` calls `collectCommitChain(repo, localHash)` and feeds the *unfiltered* result into `cherryPickOnto`. The "empty-orphan bug" is documented as the original reason disconnected histories exist in the first place (a previous bug created an empty-tree orphan root commit before the first real checkpoint landed). When `treeChangesForCherryPick` runs on a root commit, it diffs against `nil` and returns full inserts; on an empty-tree root this yields zero changes, and the `if len(changes) == 0 { continue }` in `cherryPickOnto` skips it — so the empty-orphan bug case is accidentally fine.

But a non-empty root commit will be replayed too. Concretely: imagine local was previously force-reset to a different shard layout, or an older `entire` version wrote a different tree at root. That entire tree is then layered onto the remote tip via `ApplyTreeChanges`, potentially **overwriting remote files at colliding paths**. The existing reconcile logic comments cite checkpoint shards as collision-free, but the new path now does this without the safety message ("Detected disconnected session metadata...") to stderr — the user has no idea their refs got merged.

**Suggestion:** Either (a) reuse `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch`'s empty-tree filter inside `replayDisconnectedLocalRef`, or (b) extract the filter into a shared helper. At minimum log an `Info`-level message ("replaying N local-only commits onto fetched tip after fetch found disconnected history") so the operator can correlate ref movement with the fetch event — this is exactly the "operational metadata" `logging` is for per CLAUDE.md.

Test gap that would have caught this: none of the new tests in this branch include a disconnected local chain with an empty-tree root + a real-tree child. The integration test `TestFetchMetadataBranch_DisconnectedPreservesLocalCheckpoint` only ever creates a single non-empty local commit, so the unfiltered behavior is never exercised against the documented "orphan bug" scenario.

---

## High

### H1. Behavioral change to `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` overlaps with `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` — two code paths now repair the same condition, with different policies

**Files:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:131-178`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/metadata_reconcile.go:92-199`, `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_common.go:341-432`

Pre-change, the architecture had a clean separation:
- `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef`: **never destructive** — diverged/disconnected refs were left at the local hash; readers fell through to the remote-tracking ref or v1.
- `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch`: explicitly invoked on the push path (`push_common.go:352`) with `os.Stderr` output, and from `doctor` (`doctor.go:430`). It filters empty-tree commits and prints user-visible progress.

After this branch, `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` *also* does cherry-pick-onto-target for diverged and disconnected cases. So now both:
- `fetchMetadataFromOrigin` → `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (silent replay, no filtering)
- `pushCheckpointBranch` → `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` (filtered replay, user-visible)

…will run when the same divergence pattern happens during a push. The push path runs reconcile first (which mutates the local ref to a merged state), then later calls `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` against a tmp ref — at that point local is no longer diverged from the fetched tip, so the second pass is a no-op. OK, that works by accident. But this is an extremely fragile coupling: change the order or skip the reconcile call and you'll get double-replays or conflicting policies.

**Suggestion:** Either (a) collapse `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` to delegate to the new `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (after fixing C1 to match the empty-orphan filter), or (b) document explicitly in `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef`'s doc comment that "this function is the read-side equivalent of `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch`; do not invoke both on the same fetched ref in succession". The current state has two cherry-pick paths with different filters and different output destinations doing similar work.

Also: `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef`'s new behavior on diverged refs uses different replay logic than `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` for the **diverged-but-connected** case — `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` uses `collectCommitsSince(local, base)` (excludes shared history), while `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` uses `collectCommitChain(localHash)` (the entire local chain) even though its docstring says it's "only" for disconnected. This is a latent bug in `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` not introduced here, but the divergence in semantics is now more visible.

### H2. `fullMetadataFetchArgs` silently disables `--unshallow` on open-repo errors

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:415-425`

```go
func fullMetadataFetchArgs(ctx context.Context) []string {
    repo, err := openRepository(ctx)
    if err != nil {
        return nil  // ← swallows error, fetch proceeds without --unshallow
    }
    shallowHashes, err := repo.Storer.Shallow()
    if err != nil || len(shallowHashes) == 0 {
        return nil  // ← also swallows Shallow() error
    }
    return []string{"--unshallow"}
}
```

If `openRepository` fails here, the *fetch itself* will almost certainly fail with the same error a moment later — but if there's any reason `openRepository` is transiently unhealthy while `remote.Fetch` succeeds (e.g., a stale file handle, race), you'll fetch shallowly when the caller wanted full history. The commit message for `e0834e9766` says this fixes "V2 metadata fetch after shallow refresh", which is exactly the case where missing `--unshallow` causes downstream `getV2RefTree` failures.

**Suggestion:** Return `(args, error)` and propagate. The caller (`fetchMetadataFromOrigin`) already returns an error in the same scope. At minimum, `logging.Warn` so the operator can see why `--unshallow` was skipped.

A secondary concern: `--unshallow` is only valid against the **default remote** for a refspec's source ref. The `fetchMetadataFromOrigin` and `fetchV2MainFromOrigin` paths use `fetchTarget` (resolved from "origin"), so this is fine — but if anyone later adapts this for an arbitrary URL, `--unshallow` will fail with "fatal: --unshallow on a complete repository does not make sense" or "fatal: --unshallow does not make sense with --refmap or --depth". A short comment on `fullMetadataFetchArgs` clarifying "valid only when fetching from a remote the repo was originally cloned from" would prevent that future misuse.

---

## Medium

### M1. `cherryPickOnto` skips empty deltas silently — local-only commits with no net file change vanish from the replayed chain

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/metadata_reconcile.go:499-501` (unchanged in this branch but newly relevant via the new callers in `common.go`)

```go
if len(changes) == 0 {
    continue // Skip no-op commits
}
```

The new `replayLocalCommits` relies on this behavior. For checkpoint metadata, no-op commits shouldn't happen in practice. But the new test `TestSafelyAdvanceLocalRef_Diverged_ReplaysLocalOntoTarget` doesn't exercise multi-commit replay at all — only a single local-only commit. If a local checkpoint chain has 3 commits and the middle one happens to be a no-op (e.g., a re-write of the same tree), the replayed chain will be 2 commits long with the middle's metadata/message lost. Worth a test: a 3-commit local chain → confirm all 3 replayed messages are present in the new history.

### M2. The new "TreelessFetchFails_FallsBackToFullFetch" test changed semantics under a misleading name

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/v2_resolve_test.go:99-133`

Pre-change comment said:

```
// Treeless fails, local finds it (since we wrote to the repo), so full fetch may not be called.
```

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:53` + `common_test.go:1371`

`errNoMergeBase` is `var errNoMergeBase = errors.New(...)` and `common_test.go` does `require.ErrorIs(t, mergeBaseErr, errNoMergeBase)`. That works because the test is in the same package (`strategy`). Fine. Just noting that the existing pattern in the file (`errStop`) is documented as package-scoped — a `// errNoMergeBase signals git merge-base returned "no common ancestor" via exit code 1.` comment would match style.

---

## Nits

### N1. Two-step `if errors.Is(err, errNoMergeBase) { ... } if err != nil { ... }` reads awkwardly

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/common.go:156-169`

```go
mergeBase, err := getMergeBase(ctx, repoPath, localHash.String(), targetHash.String())
if errors.Is(err, errNoMergeBase) {
    // disconnected path
    return replayDisconnectedLocalRef(...)
}
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("failed to find merge base for %s: %w", localRefName, err)
}
```

`switch` on the error or extracting the disconnected-path handling into a helper that takes the `error` would read more linearly. Stylistic only.

### N2. `fullMetadataFetchArgs(ctx)` is called with a context that may already be `context.WithTimeout`-wrapped to 2 minutes, and the function does a synchronous `openRepository`

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli/cmd/entire/cli/git_operations.go:415-425, 432-456`

`fetchMetadataFromOrigin` calls `context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Minute)` then immediately calls `fullMetadataFetchArgs(ctx)`. Subtle: the open is fast in practice, but it's now inside the 2-minute fetch budget. If `openRepository` ever does anything network-y (it doesn't today), this would compete with the fetch budget. Move the `fullMetadataFetchArgs` call *before* the context wrap if you want the open to be independent.

### N3. The diff renames `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef`'s old doc-comment ("diverged is the dangerous one this guard exists for") rather than amending it to reflect the policy reversal

The new comment correctly describes the new behavior, but `git blame` will show the old defender-of-local-commits commentary disappearing in a 7-commit branch where the very first commit changes the semantic to replay-onto-target. A reader doing archaeology will need to read both states to understand the design evolution. Not actionable in this PR but the design rationale (why we changed from preserve to replay) belongs in a code comment or design doc.

---

## Praise

- **Shallow guard (commit 60298e7092)** is genuinely good defensive programming: refusing to replay when the algorithm cannot prove the histories are disconnected is the right choice over silently doing the wrong thing. The 10s timeout and shallowHashes shortcut for non-shallow repos are nice details.
- **Pivot from "preserve local only" to "replay onto target"** is a real upgrade for the user-facing scenario described ("checkpoint metadata produced on another machine"). The previous policy left readers in a fall-through state that produced confusing UX.
- **`tryFullFetch` closure in `v2_resolve.go`** with the `fullFetchTried` flag is a clean refactor — eliminates an awkward "did we already try?" check across two code paths.
- **Consistent error-handling pattern in the three `ensure*` functions** (`committed.go:1685`, `v2_store.go:86`, `trail/store.go:46`) is precisely the right fix: previously a transient/malformed-ref error was indistinguishable from "branch missing → create it", which could create a duplicate orphan root. All three sites are correct and identically structured.
- **`TestFetchMetadataBranch_DivergedPreservesLocalCheckpoint`** is a thorough E2E-style test: it sets up real bare-repo + clone, performs the actual fetch path, and verifies the *post-state* ref parent chain. This is the right shape for testing the bug class.
- **`getMergeBase` exit-code-1 handling** correctly distinguishes "no merge base" (exit 1) from "fatal" (exit 128).

---

- Tests and lint **pass cleanly**.
- The branch addresses a real and previously dangerous bug (force-fetch overwriting local checkpoint commits).
- **Blocker: C1** — the new disconnected-replay path doesn't filter empty-tree commits the way the existing `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` does. Either share the filter or document why it's not needed here.
- **Should-fix: H1, H2, M2** — the architectural overlap with `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` deserves at least a doc comment, the `--unshallow` arg generator should propagate errors, and the v2_resolve fallback-order change deserves a doc note.
- Most other findings are polish or test-quality observations.

**Estimated effort to address: 1–3 hours** (mostly C1 + adding 1–2 tests for multi-commit and empty-tree-root replay scenarios; H2 is a one-line propagation change).

## Review of `config-perm` vs `origin/main`

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES** — one critical correctness issue plus a tangled overlap with existing code.

Lint and tests pass cleanly. The branch genuinely fixes a real bug (force-fetch overwriting local checkpoint commits) but has rough edges.

### Critical
- **C1 — `replayDisconnectedLocalRef` skips the empty-tree filter** that `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` applies (`strategy/common.go:188-194` vs `metadata_reconcile.go:157-172`). On a disconnected local chain rooted at a non-empty "orphan-bug" commit, the entire tree gets layered onto the fetched tip via `ApplyTreeChanges`, potentially overwriting remote files at colliding paths — silently, since there's no logging. Reuse the filter or extract it as a shared helper.

### High
- **H1 — Two cherry-pick paths for the same condition** now exist: `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (new, silent, unfiltered) and `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` (push/doctor, filtered, logs to stderr). The push path runs both in succession; works only because the first mutates the ref so the second becomes a no-op. Either collapse them or document the coupling on both functions.
- **H2 — `fullMetadataFetchArgs` swallows `openRepository` errors** (`git_operations.go:415-425`), silently skipping `--unshallow` if the open hiccups — exactly the case commit `e0834e9766` was meant to fix. Propagate the error.

### Medium
- **M1 — `cherryPickOnto` drops no-op deltas**; new tests don't cover multi-commit replay where a middle commit happens to be a no-op (lost metadata/message).
- **M2 — `v2_resolve.go` now always does a full fetch after treeless failure**, even when local has data. Real behavior change buried in a test rename; deserves a doc-comment on `GetV2MetadataTree`.
- **M3 — Shallow-history error message** ("reachable shallow history prevents proving refs are disconnected") leaks an internal concept with no remediation hint. Reword to point at `entire doctor` / `git fetch --unshallow`.

### Low
- **L1** — `TestSafelyAdvanceLocalRef_DoesNotAdvanceOnRefReadError` still uses file-local `initTestRepo` (raw `git.PlainInit`) instead of `testutil.InitRepo` per CLAUDE.md.
- **L2** — New `checkpointRemote*` test helpers duplicate logic available via `testutil`.
- **L3** — Two new tests use `t.Chdir` and skip `t.Parallel()`. TODO: thread `repoPath` through `FetchMetadataBranch`.
- **L4** — `historyReachesShallowBoundary` runs unbounded `git rev-list`; should cap with `--max-count=MaxCommitTraversalDepth`.
- **L5** — `errNoMergeBase` lacks a doc comment (existing file pattern documents sentinels).

### Praise
The shallow-history guard (60298e7092) is good defensive programming, the `tryFullFetch` closure refactor is clean, and the three identical `ensure*` fixes (`committed.go`, `v2_store.go`, `trail/store.go`) are correct in all three sites. The diverged-preserves-local-checkpoint test is a proper E2E-shaped test.

**Effort to address: ~1–3 hours** (C1 fix + 1–2 missing tests + the H2 one-liner).

Full reviewer agent report retained in context (agent id `acbc08a789365cec5`) — let me know if you want me to implement any of these or push back on findings.

{"additions":332,"body":"## Summary

Two related fixes for `entire resume` and the underlying ref-advance helper. They compose: the second hardens the helper so the first is fully safe in every scenario.

### 1. Fix the user-visible bug (`resume.go`)
`promoteRemoteTrackingMetadataBranch` returned early whenever the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` ref existed — even when `origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` was ahead. The committed-checkpoint store used by `RestoreLogsOnly` and `resumeSingleSession` only falls back to `refs/remotes/origin/...` when the local ref is **missing**, so `entire resume` printed "session log not available" for checkpoints already in the remote-tracking ref.

Drop the early return so `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` runs unconditionally — same pattern `FetchMetadataBranch` already uses after a real fetch.

### 2. Protect unpushed local commits in `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` (`strategy/common.go`)
The previous contract overwrote any local ref the target couldn't reach, which silently discarded unpushed local commits whenever a fetch landed sibling commits — e.g. checkpoint metadata produced on another machine sharing the same orphan-style refs (`entire/checkpoints/v1`, the V2 main ref). The objects survived in the loose-objects pool until git gc, but the branch ref no longer pointed at them.

Tighten the helper so it only sets the ref when the move is non-destructive:
- missing → create
- local at/ahead of target → no-op (existing protection)
- local strictly behind target → fast-forward
- diverged or unrelated history → no-op with a debug log

All three production callers (`promoteRemoteTrackingMetadataBranch`, `FetchMetadataBranch`, `PromoteTmpRefSafely`) sync orphan branches where this is the correct semantic. In the rare divergent case, resume falls through to remote-tracking-tree reads (v1) or the DualCheckpointReader → V1 fallback.

`TestFetchV2MainFromURL_UpdatesExistingRef` was updated to use the existing `advanceV2MainOnTop` helper — the prior setup advanced via a second call to `createV2MainRef` (always an unrelated orphan commit), which was only "working" via the now-removed diverged-overwrite path. content.text:
Looking at PR #1252 + config-perm together, the design evolved through three states:
1. **Original (buggy)**: force-fetch overwrites local checkpoints → data loss
2. **PR #1252**: `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` refuses to advance when diverged/unrelated → local preserved but ignored by readers
3. **config-perm**: replays local commits onto fetched tip → histories merge

That progression has a lot of edge cases worth pinning down with tests. Here's a draft plan.

## Test Plan: Checkpoint Ref Sync Scenarios

### Where these go
All as **integration tests** in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/` using the existing `NewFeatureBranchEnv` + `SetupBareRemote` infrastructure (which simulates hooks without real agents). Two scenarios get **non-agent E2E tests** in `e2e/tests/` for CLI-level wiring (real `entire` binary, real `git push`/`pull`). No agent invocations.

### Group A — Fetch/replay correctness (the config-perm pivot)

| # | Test | Scenario | Why |
|---|------|----------|-----|
| A1 | `TestFetchMetadata_DivergedLocal_ReplaysOntoRemote` | Local chain `A→B`, origin advances to `A→C` (sibling). After fetch, local ref is rooted at `C` with `B`'s tree applied on top; `entire explain` finds both checkpoints. | Locks the new replay-on-divergence behavior end-to-end. |
| A2 | `TestFetchMetadata_DisconnectedNonEmptyRoot_FiltersOrphan` | Local has `[empty-tree-root, real-commit]`, origin has independent chain. After fetch, only the real commit's tree appears on the replayed tip — empty root is filtered. | **Covers review finding C1.** Currently no test forces this; the new `replayDisconnectedLocalRef` lacks the filter `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` has. |
| A3 | `TestFetchMetadata_DisconnectedMultiCommit_PreservesOrder` | Local chain has 3 real commits with distinguishable metadata. After replay, all 3 messages and trees are present in the same order. | **Covers review M1.** Today's tests only exercise single-commit replay. |
| A4 | `TestFetchMetadata_ShallowClone_DisconnectedRefusesReplay` | Clone with `--depth=1`, manufacture a local checkpoint commit whose history can't reach the shallow boundary. Fetch must NOT replay (would silently merge unrelated histories). Error message includes a remediation hint. | Verifies the new `historyReachesShallowBoundary` guard and surfaces review M3 (error wording). |
| A5 | `TestV2MetadataFetch_AfterShallowRefresh_SucceedsViaUnshallow` | V2 main ref present on origin, local clone is shallow, `GetV2MetadataTree` triggers full fetch and `getV2RefTree` succeeds. | Locks commit `e0834e9766`. |

### Group B — `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` contract (locks PR #1252)

These exist in unit form but not as integration tests against a real bare-remote round-trip.

| # | Test | Scenario |
|---|------|----------|
| B1 | `TestSafelyAdvance_MissingLocal_CreatedFromRemote` | First fetch on a fresh clone — local ref created. |
| B2 | `TestSafelyAdvance_LocalAhead_NoOp` | Local has unpushed checkpoints, origin is behind, fetch leaves local untouched. |
| B3 | `TestSafelyAdvance_LocalBehind_FastForwards` | The original PR #1252 user-visible bug. Reproduces "session log not available" if the fix regressed. |

### Group C — Resume / cross-machine (non-agent E2E)

These are the user-facing scenarios. Use real `entire` binary, two clones of a bare remote.

| # | Test | Scenario |
|---|------|----------|
| C1 | `e2e/tests/resume_remote_diverged_test.go: TestResume_DivergedCheckpoints_FindsBothSessions` | Machine A commits a checkpoint and pushes. Machine B (separate clone) commits a checkpoint without pulling, pushes (force-with-lease blocked — so we test what happens after they pull). After A pulls B's push, A can `entire resume` either session. |
| C2 | `e2e/tests/resume_remote_stale_test.go: TestResume_StaleLocalMetadata_RestoresViaRemote` | Origin has more checkpoints than local. `entire resume <session-id>` succeeds (the PR #1252 user-visible bug, now end-to-end). |

### Group D — Push path interaction (review H1)

| # | Test | Scenario |
|---|------|----------|
| D1 | `TestPush_AfterDivergedFetch_NoDoubleReplay` | After A1's setup, run `pushCheckpointBranch`. Verify `ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch` does the work and the subsequent `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` call is a no-op (the implicit coupling the review flagged). Inspect commit count on the resulting branch — must equal the merged-history count, not double. |

### Group E — Negative / error surface (review M3)

| # | Test | Scenario |
|---|------|----------|
| E1 | `TestFetchMetadata_ShallowBoundary_ErrorMessageActionable` | Same setup as A4; assert the error contains the user-actionable hint (`git fetch --unshallow` or `entire doctor`), not just the internal phrase "reachable shallow history prevents proving refs are disconnected". |

### Branch / PR structure
- **Branch name**: `test/checkpoint-ref-sync-scenarios` off `main` (clean base — `config-perm` is unmerged and `main` already has #1252).
- **Single PR**, organized as commits:
  1. Group A (5 tests) — most important, covers the active regression risk
  2. Group B (3 tests) — locks the merged PR #1252 contract
  3. Group C (2 E2E tests)
  4. Group D + E (2 tests)
- Each test calls `t.Parallel()` unless it uses `t.Chdir` (cross-machine E2E ones will).
- Use `testutil.InitRepo` + existing `NewFeatureBranchEnv` helpers; no raw `git.PlainInit`.

### Open questions before I start

641	// exists on the remote, it needs full blob content (source files) — not a
642	// partial clone.

645	// to a bare remote, then clones to a fresh repo that does NOT have the

662		// locally so it only exists on the remote. This forces resume to fetch it.
663		cloneEnv := env.CloneFrom(bareDir)
664	
665		ctx := t.Context()
666	
667		// Detach HEAD so we can delete the feature branch.
668		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "checkout", "--detach")
669		cmd.Dir = cloneEnv.RepoDir
670		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
671		if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {

673		}
674	
675		cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "branch", "-D", "feature/test-branch")
676		cmd.Dir = cloneEnv.RepoDir
677		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
678		if output, err := cmd.CombinedOutput(); err != nil {

694		}

697		// With filtered_fetches enabled, the fetch must still be unfiltered so the
698		// source file blob (auth.go) is available after checkout.

func TestFetchMetadataBranch_DoesNotRewindLocalAhead(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()

	// Set up remote with metadata branch at commit A.
	remoteDir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, remoteDir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, remoteDir, "f.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, remoteDir, "f.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, remoteDir, "init")

	branchCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
	branchCmd.Dir = remoteDir
	branchCmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	branchOut, err := branchCmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defaultBranch := strings.TrimSpace(string(branchOut))

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "checkout", "--orphan", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
	cmd.Dir = remoteDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rm", "-rf", ".")
	cmd.Dir = remoteDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	testutil.WriteFile(t, remoteDir, "metadata.json", `{"checkpoint": "A"}`)
	testutil.GitAdd(t, remoteDir, "metadata.json")
	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-m", "checkpoint A")
	cmd.Dir = remoteDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "checkout", defaultBranch)
	cmd.Dir = remoteDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	// Set up local repo and fetch once so local metadata branch is at A.
	localDir := t.TempDir()
	testutil.InitRepo(t, localDir)
	testutil.WriteFile(t, localDir, "f.txt", "init")
	testutil.GitAdd(t, localDir, "f.txt")
	testutil.GitCommit(t, localDir, "init")
	t.Chdir(localDir)

	require.NoError(t, FetchMetadataBranch(ctx, remoteDir))

	hashCmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
	hashCmd.Dir = localDir
	hashCmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	aOut, err := hashCmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	aHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(aOut))

	// Advance local metadata branch to B (ahead of remote), without pushing.
	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "checkout", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
	cmd.Dir = localDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	testutil.WriteFile(t, localDir, "metadata.json", `{"checkpoint": "B"}`)
	testutil.GitAdd(t, localDir, "metadata.json")
	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-m", "checkpoint B")
	cmd.Dir = localDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	hashCmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
	hashCmd.Dir = localDir
	hashCmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	bOut, err := hashCmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	bHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(bOut))
	require.NotEqual(t, aHash, bHash, "test setup: local should have advanced beyond remote tip")

	// Go back to default branch — matches how the CLI runs this codepath.
	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "checkout", defaultBranch)
	cmd.Dir = localDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())

	// Fetch again — must NOT rewind local from B to A.
	require.NoError(t, FetchMetadataBranch(ctx, remoteDir))

	hashCmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "entire/checkpoints/v1")
	hashCmd.Dir = localDir
	hashCmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	afterOut, err := hashCmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	afterHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(afterOut))

	assert.Equal(t, bHash, afterHash,
		"FetchMetadataBranch must not rewind locally-ahead metadata branch; expected %s (B), got %s (A=%s)",
		bHash, afterHash, aHash)
}

// v2RefSeq is a counter to ensure each call to createV2MainRef produces a distinct commit.
var v2RefSeq int

// createV2MainRef creates a v2 /main custom ref with a single orphan commit.
// Uses git plumbing to create the ref under refs/entire/ (not refs/heads/).
// Each call produces a distinct commit (uses a sequence counter in content).
func createV2MainRef(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir string) {
	t.Helper()
	v2RefSeq++

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "hash-object", "-w", "--stdin")
	cmd.Dir = repoDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader(fmt.Sprintf(`{"test": true, "seq": %d}`, v2RefSeq))
	blobOut, err := cmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	blobHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(blobOut))

	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "mktree")
	cmd.Dir = repoDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	cmd.Stdin = strings.NewReader("100644 blob " + blobHash + "\tmetadata.json\n")
	treeOut, err := cmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	treeHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(treeOut))

	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "commit-tree", "-m", fmt.Sprintf("v2 checkpoint %d", v2RefSeq), treeHash)
	cmd.Dir = repoDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	commitOut, err := cmd.Output()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	commitHash := strings.TrimSpace(string(commitOut))

	cmd = exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "update-ref", paths.V2MainRefName, commitHash)
	cmd.Dir = repoDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	require.NoError(t, cmd.Run())
}

// refExists checks whether a custom ref exists in the repo.
func refExists(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, refName string) bool {
	t.Helper()
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "show-ref", "--verify", "--quiet", refName)
	cmd.Dir = repoDir
	cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
	return cmd.Run() == nil
}

func TestFetchMetadataBranch_DisconnectedMultiCommit_PreservesAllLocalData(t *testing.T) {
	env := newCheckpointBranchEnv(t)
	ctx := env.ctx

	// Remote: single root R, disconnected from local. Use a distinct filename
	// ("remote-only.json") so we can verify remote data is reachable from the
	// merged tip -- the preserve-on-divergence path leaves the test passing
	// vacuously on local data alone, so we anchor the assertion on remote.
	rHash := createCheckpointOrphanRoot(t, ctx, env.remoteDir, env.defaultBranch, "R")
	appendCheckpointCommit(t, ctx, env.remoteDir, env.defaultBranch,
		"remote-only.json", `{"side":"remote"}`)

	// Local: three-commit chain L1 -> L2 -> L3, each adding a distinct file.
	createCheckpointOrphanRoot(t, ctx, env.localDir, env.defaultBranch, "L1")
	appendCheckpointCommit(t, ctx, env.localDir, env.defaultBranch, "l2.json", `{"step":2}`)
	appendCheckpointCommit(t, ctx, env.localDir, env.defaultBranch, "l3.json", `{"step":3}`)

	t.Chdir(env.localDir)
	require.NoError(t, FetchMetadataBranch(ctx, env.remoteDir))

	tipHash := getRefHash(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName)
	reachable := reachableHashes(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName)
	assert.Contains(t, reachable, rHash,
		"remote root R should be reachable from the merged tip after multi-commit replay; tip=%s", tipHash)

	// All three local files must be readable from the merged tip's tree.
	root := readBlobAtRef(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName, "metadata.json")
	assert.Contains(t, root, "L1", "L1's metadata.json must survive replay")

	step2 := readBlobAtRef(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName, "l2.json")
	assert.Contains(t, step2, "2", "L2's file must survive replay")

	step3 := readBlobAtRef(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName, "l3.json")
	assert.Contains(t, step3, "3", "L3's file must survive replay")

	// And the remote-only file must also be reachable.
	remote := readBlobAtRef(t, ctx, env.localDir, paths.MetadataBranchName, "remote-only.json")
	assert.Contains(t, remote, "remote", "remote-only.json must be reachable after multi-commit replay")
}

3	// These tests focus on the FetchMetadataBranch behavior when the local
4	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ref diverges from (or has no shared history with) the
5	// remote tip. They are paired with the existing fast-forward / no-rewind
6	// contract tests in checkpoint_remote_test.go:
7	//
8	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_FetchesAndCreatesLocalBranch  -- missing local
9	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_UpdatesExistingLocalBranch    -- local strictly behind
10	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_DoesNotRewindLocalAhead       -- local strictly ahead
11	//
12	// The scenarios here cover the cases above and beyond fast-forward:
13	//   - local diverged from remote (sibling commits sharing a base)
14	//   - local disconnected from remote (no common ancestor)
15	//   - multi-commit local chains
16	//   - empty-tree orphan-root pollution
17	//   - shallow-clone boundaries that hide ancestry
18	//
19	// Several of these tests document behavior introduced by the in-flight
20	// "replay local checkpoints when fetch finds a diverged remote" work and will
21	// fail against the current main contract (which preserves but does not replay
22	// diverged local refs). That is intentional -- they serve as an executable
23	// specification of the target behavior.
24	
25	import (
26		"context"
27		"fmt"
28		"os/exec"
29		"strings"
30		"testing"
31	
32		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/paths"
33		"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil"
34	
35		"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
36		"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
37	)
38	
39	// ---- shared scaffolding ----------------------------------------------------
40	
41	// checkpointBranchEnv holds the two repos a fetch test needs: a "remote"
42	// where the entire/checkpoints/v1 orphan branch is built, and a "local" that
43	// will run FetchMetadataBranch against it.
44	type checkpointBranchEnv struct {
45		t             *testing.T
46		ctx           context.Context
47		remoteDir     string
48		localDir      string
49		defaultBranch string
50	}
51	
52	// newCheckpointBranchEnv initializes both repos with a trivial commit on the
53	// default branch so they have an established working-branch HEAD that fetches
54	// won't disturb.
55	func newCheckpointBranchEnv(t *testing.T) *checkpointBranchEnv {
56		t.Helper()
57		ctx := context.Background()
58	
59		remoteDir := t.TempDir()
60		testutil.InitRepo(t, remoteDir)
61		testutil.WriteFile(t, remoteDir, "f.txt", "init")
62		testutil.GitAdd(t, remoteDir, "f.txt")
63		testutil.GitCommit(t, remoteDir, "init")
64	
65		localDir := t.TempDir()
66		testutil.InitRepo(t, localDir)
67		testutil.WriteFile(t, localDir, "f.txt", "init")
68		testutil.GitAdd(t, localDir, "f.txt")
69		testutil.GitCommit(t, localDir, "init")
70	
71		defaultBranch := repoCurrentBranch(ctx, t, remoteDir)
72		require.NotEmpty(t, defaultBranch, "default branch should be set on fresh repo")
73		require.Equal(t, defaultBranch, repoCurrentBranch(ctx, t, localDir),
74			"remote and local should share the same default branch name for predictable test setup")
75	
76		return &checkpointBranchEnv{
77			t:             t,
78			ctx:           ctx,
79			remoteDir:     remoteDir,
80			localDir:      localDir,
81			defaultBranch: defaultBranch,
82		}
83	}
84	
85	func repoCurrentBranch(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir string) string {
86		t.Helper()
87		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
88		cmd.Dir = repoDir
89		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
90		out, err := cmd.Output()
91		require.NoError(t, err)
92		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
93	}
94	
95	// createCheckpointOrphanRoot creates a fresh entire/checkpoints/v1 orphan
96	// branch in repoDir with a single root commit containing a metadata.json file.
97	// Returns the commit hash. Leaves HEAD on the default branch.
98	func createCheckpointOrphanRoot(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch, label string) string {
99		t.Helper()
100	
101		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", "--orphan", paths.MetadataBranchName)
102		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "rm", "-rf", ".")
103	
104		contents := fmt.Sprintf(`{"checkpoint": %q}`, label)
105		testutil.WriteFile(t, repoDir, "metadata.json", contents)
106		testutil.GitAdd(t, repoDir, "metadata.json")
107		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-m", "checkpoint "+label)
108	
109		hash := getRefHash(ctx, t, repoDir, paths.MetadataBranchName)
110		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", defaultBranch)
111		return hash
112	}
113	
114	// appendCheckpointCommit adds a checkpoint commit on top of the current
115	// metadata-branch tip in repoDir. fileName/contents distinguish commits in
116	// assertions. Returns the new commit hash. HEAD is restored to defaultBranch.
117	func appendCheckpointCommit(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch, fileName, contents string) string {
118		t.Helper()
119	
120		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", paths.MetadataBranchName)
121		testutil.WriteFile(t, repoDir, fileName, contents)
122		testutil.GitAdd(t, repoDir, fileName)
123		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-m", "checkpoint "+fileName)
124	
125		hash := getRefHash(ctx, t, repoDir, paths.MetadataBranchName)
126		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", defaultBranch)
127		return hash
128	}
129	
130	// createOrphanRootWithEmptyTree creates an empty-tree root commit on the
131	// metadata branch in repoDir -- reproduces the historical "orphan-bug" commit
132	// shape that filtering logic must skip during replay. Returns the commit
133	// hash. Leaves HEAD on defaultBranch.
134	func createOrphanRootWithEmptyTree(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch string) string {
135		t.Helper()
136	
137		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", "--orphan", paths.MetadataBranchName)
138		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "rm", "-rf", ".")
139		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "empty orphan root")
140	
141		hash := getRefHash(ctx, t, repoDir, paths.MetadataBranchName)
142		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", defaultBranch)
143		return hash
144	}
145	
146	func runGit(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) {
147		t.Helper()
148		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
149		cmd.Dir = dir
150		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
151		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
152		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git %s failed: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), out)
153	}
154	
155	func getRefHash(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, refName string) string {
156		t.Helper()
157		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", refName)
158		cmd.Dir = repoDir
159		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
160		out, err := cmd.Output()
161		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git rev-parse %s failed in %s", refName, repoDir)
162		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
163	}
164	
165	// reachableHashes returns every commit reachable from the given ref in repoDir,
166	// using `git rev-list`. Order is newest-first, matching git's default.
167	func reachableHashes(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, ref string) []string {
168		t.Helper()
169		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", ref)
170		cmd.Dir = repoDir
171		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
172		out, err := cmd.Output()
173		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git rev-list %s failed in %s", ref, repoDir)
174		hashes := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n")
175		if len(hashes) == 1 && hashes[0] == "" {
176			return nil
177		}
178		return hashes
179	}
180	
181	// readBlobAtRef returns the contents of path at the given ref, or "" if absent.
182	func readBlobAtRef(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, ref, path string) string {
183		t.Helper()
184		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "show", ref+":"+path)
185		cmd.Dir = repoDir
186		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
187		out, err := cmd.Output()
188		if err != nil {
189			return ""
190		}
191		return string(out)
192	}
193

3	// These tests focus on the FetchMetadataBranch behavior when the local
4	// entire/checkpoints/v1 ref diverges from (or has no shared history with) the
5	// remote tip. They are paired with the existing fast-forward / no-rewind
6	// contract tests in checkpoint_remote_test.go:
7	//
8	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_FetchesAndCreatesLocalBranch  -- missing local
9	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_UpdatesExistingLocalBranch    -- local strictly behind
10	//   TestFetchMetadataBranch_DoesNotRewindLocalAhead       -- local strictly ahead
11	//
12	// The scenarios here cover the cases above and beyond fast-forward:
13	//   - local diverged from remote (sibling commits sharing a base)
14	//   - local disconnected from remote (no common ancestor)
15	//   - multi-commit local chains
16	//   - empty-tree orphan-root pollution
17	//   - shallow-clone boundaries that hide ancestry
18	//
19	// Several of these tests document behavior introduced by the in-flight
20	// "replay local checkpoints when fetch finds a diverged remote" work and will
21	// fail against the current main contract (which preserves but does not replay
22	// diverged local refs). That is intentional -- they serve as an executable
23	// specification of the target behavior.

41	// checkpointBranchEnv holds the two repos a fetch test needs: a "remote"
42	// where the entire/checkpoints/v1 orphan branch is built, and a "local" that
43	// will run FetchMetadataBranch against it.
44	type checkpointBranchEnv struct {
45		t             *testing.T
46		ctx           context.Context
47		remoteDir     string
48		localDir      string
49		defaultBranch string
50	}

52	// newCheckpointBranchEnv initializes both repos with a trivial commit on the
53	// default branch so they have an established working-branch HEAD that fetches
54	// won't disturb.
55	func newCheckpointBranchEnv(t *testing.T) *checkpointBranchEnv {
56		t.Helper()
57		ctx := context.Background()
58	
59		remoteDir := t.TempDir()
60		testutil.InitRepo(t, remoteDir)
61		testutil.WriteFile(t, remoteDir, "f.txt", "init")
62		testutil.GitAdd(t, remoteDir, "f.txt")
63		testutil.GitCommit(t, remoteDir, "init")
64	
65		localDir := t.TempDir()
66		testutil.InitRepo(t, localDir)
67		testutil.WriteFile(t, localDir, "f.txt", "init")
68		testutil.GitAdd(t, localDir, "f.txt")
69		testutil.GitCommit(t, localDir, "init")
70	
71		defaultBranch := repoCurrentBranch(ctx, t, remoteDir)
72		require.NotEmpty(t, defaultBranch, "default branch should be set on fresh repo")
73		require.Equal(t, defaultBranch, repoCurrentBranch(ctx, t, localDir),
74			"remote and local should share the same default branch name for predictable test setup")
75	
76		return &checkpointBranchEnv{
77			t:             t,
78			ctx:           ctx,
79			remoteDir:     remoteDir,
80			localDir:      localDir,
81			defaultBranch: defaultBranch,
82		}
83	}

85	func repoCurrentBranch(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir string) string {
86		t.Helper()
87		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", "--abbrev-ref", "HEAD")
88		cmd.Dir = repoDir
89		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
90		out, err := cmd.Output()
91		require.NoError(t, err)
92		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
93	}

95	// createCheckpointOrphanRoot creates a fresh entire/checkpoints/v1 orphan
96	// branch in repoDir with a single root commit containing a metadata.json file.
97	// Returns the commit hash. Leaves HEAD on the default branch.
98	func createCheckpointOrphanRoot(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch, label string) string {

108

111		return hash
112	}

115	// metadata-branch tip in repoDir. fileName/contents distinguish commits in
116	// assertions. Returns the new commit hash. HEAD is restored to defaultBranch.
117	func appendCheckpointCommit(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch, fileName, contents string) string {

119

123		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "-m", "checkpoint "+fileName)

131	// metadata branch in repoDir -- reproduces the historical "orphan-bug" commit
132	// shape that filtering logic must skip during replay. Returns the commit
133	// hash. Leaves HEAD on defaultBranch.
134	func createOrphanRootWithEmptyTree(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, defaultBranch string) string {
135		t.Helper()
136	
137		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", "--orphan", paths.MetadataBranchName)
138		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "rm", "-rf", ".")
139		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "-c", "commit.gpgsign=false", "commit", "--allow-empty", "-m", "empty orphan root")
140	
141		hash := getMetadataBranchHash(ctx, t, repoDir)
142		runGit(ctx, t, repoDir, "checkout", defaultBranch)
143		return hash
144	}

146	func runGit(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, dir string, args ...string) {
147		t.Helper()
148		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", args...)
149		cmd.Dir = dir
150		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
151		out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
152		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git %s failed: %s", strings.Join(args, " "), out)
153	}

155	func getMetadataBranchHash(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir string) string {
156		t.Helper()
157		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-parse", paths.MetadataBranchName)
158		cmd.Dir = repoDir
159		cmd.Env = testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()
160		out, err := cmd.Output()
161		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git rev-parse %s failed in %s", paths.MetadataBranchName, repoDir)
162		return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
163	}

166	// branch tip in repoDir. Order is newest-first, matching git rev-list default.
167	func metadataBranchReachable(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir string) []string {
168		t.Helper()
169		cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "rev-list", paths.MetadataBranchName)
170		cmd.Dir = repoDir

173		require.NoErrorf(t, err, "git rev-list %s failed in %s", paths.MetadataBranchName, repoDir)
174		hashes := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n")
175		if len(hashes) == 1 && hashes[0] == "" {
176			return nil
177		}
178		return hashes
179	}
180

182	// branch tip in repoDir, or "" if absent.
183	func readBlobOnMetadataBranch(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, repoDir, path string) string {

Add cross-machine resume + push-replay integration tests

Two CLI-level integration tests covering the cross-machine scenarios
the strategy-package tests don't reach:

TestResume_StaleLocalMetadata_RemoteHasNewerCheckpoint reproduces the
PR #1252 user-visible bug end-to-end via the real CLI binary: when the
local entire/checkpoints/v1 ref is behind refs/remotes/origin/... after
another machine pushed, `entire session resume <branch>` printed
"session log not available" for the newer checkpoint. The unit-level
TestResumeFromCurrentBranch_FastForwardsStaleLocalMetadata covers the
same path with a direct function call; this one catches wiring
regressions the unit test would miss.

TestPushAfterDiverged_NoDoubleReplayCommits guards against the
architectural concern raised in the config-perm review (finding H1):
if both fetchMetadataFromOrigin -> SafelyAdvanceLocalRef AND
pushCheckpointBranch -> ReconcileDisconnectedMetadataBranch run during
a single push retry, the merged history could contain a replayed
commit twice. Asserts exactly 3 commits on the metadata branch after
the divergence-then-push flow (root + A + B rebased); a double-replay
would produce 4.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

## Summary

Adds 7 new tests covering the FetchMetadataBranch behavior introduced by PR #1252 and the in-flight replay work in the `config-perm` branch. Pairs with the existing fast-forward / no-rewind contract tests in `checkpoint_remote_test.go`.

## Tests

### `cmd/entire/cli/strategy/replay_disconnected_test.go` (Groups A + E)

| Test | Status on `main` | What it locks |
|---|---|---|
| `TestFetchMetadataBranch_DivergedLocal_ReplaysOntoRemote` | **FAIL** | Local A→B, origin A→C → after fetch local must reach C with B's tree applied. Reproduces the gap PR #1252 left open. |
| `TestFetchMetadataBranch_DisconnectedEmptyRoot_FiltersOrphan` | **FAIL** | Disconnected local rooted at an empty-tree "orphan-bug" commit; the empty root must be filtered before replay. (Review finding C1.) |
| `TestFetchMetadataBranch_DisconnectedMultiCommit_PreservesAllLocalData` | **FAIL** | 3-commit local chain + disconnected remote — all 3 local files AND the remote tip must be reachable. (Review finding M1.) |
| `TestFetchMetadataBranch_ShallowClone_RefusesReplayAcrossBoundary` | PASS | Shallow boundary hides ancestry — fetch must not silently merge unrelated histories. Permits either "error" or "no-op preserve" as safe outcomes. |
| `TestFetchMetadataBranch_ShallowBoundary_ErrorIsActionable` | SKIP | When the shallow case surfaces an error, it must mention `doctor` / `--unshallow` (review M3). Skips on `main` since no error is raised. |

### `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/diverged_replay_test.go` (Groups C + D)

{"body":"<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/414
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` only short-circuited when local was equal to or strictly ahead of `targetHash`; every other state (missing, behind, diverged, disconnected) flowed into the same `SetReference` call.

That was correct for "missing" (initialize) and "behind" (fast-forward), because targetHash already contains everything reachable from local. It was wrong for the diverged and disconnected cases: local-only checkpoint commits that hadn't been pushed yet were left as orphans the moment any caller (resume, doctor, the read-side metadata fetch) advanced the local ref to a remote tip that didn't contain them.

Split the post-equality branch on git-merge-base instead:
```
  mergeBase == targetHash  -> local ahead, no-op
  mergeBase == localHash   -> local behind, fast-forward (unchanged)
  mergeBase exists, neither -> diverged, cherryPickOnto local-only commits
  errNoMergeBase            -> disconnected, cherryPickOnto full local chain
```
The fast-forward path still goes through the same `setRefHash` call as before, so the existing "behind" behavior is preserved by construction. The diverged and disconnected paths now replay local-only commits onto targetHash via `cherryPickOnto`, which preserves the original Author and stamps the local user as Committer.

getMergeBase gained an errNoMergeBase sentinel so exit-1 ("no common ancestor") is distinguishable from a real git failure and can route to the disconnected-replay path instead of bubbling up as an error.

Regression tests under `FetchMetadataBranch` cover the diverged and disconnected cases and assert that the local-only checkpoint blob is still in the tree after the fetch.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how local refs are advanced during checkpoint metadata fetches by cherry-picking local-only commits onto fetched tips, which affects git history manipulation and could mis-handle edge cases in unusual repo states.
> 
> **Overview**
> Prevents `FetchMetadataBranch` from orphaning unpushed local checkpoints when the local metadata branch is *diverged* or *disconnected* from the fetched remote tip.
> 
> `SafelyAdvanceLocalRef` is updated to compute a merge-base with the fetched target and, when necessary, **replay local-only commits onto the fetched tip** (via `cherryPickOnto`) instead of overwriting the ref; it also adds a `errNoMergeBase` sentinel and teaches `getMergeBase` to surface the "no common ancestor" case distinctly.
> 
> Adds regression tests covering diverged and disconnected fetch scenarios, asserting that local-only checkpoint blobs remain present after fetch and that the resulting branch tip reflects a replay onto the remote tip.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e07f38396796408f0e1c9947ab5f6268a097bfe6. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

122		if localCount != 3 {

125		}
126
